sections.summary: New `folderOpenSettle.ts` module (LIVE_SNAPSHOT_DEADLINE_MS 400, OPEN_SPINNER_DELAY_MS 80, `isLiveSnapshot`, `reportAppliedSnapshot`, `waitForLiveSnapshot`). App.tsx: `applySnapshot` reports every applied snapshot's stage; the three open handlers share `adoptOpenedSnapshot`; the two picker-driven opens funnel through `openThroughPicker`, which keeps `openingRecentPath` set — and so the picker mounted — until a `stage === 'live'` snapshot for that root lands or 400 ms pass, then closes it; `FolderChromeButton onSelect` no longer closes up front. `skeletonOpenRootRef` arms the skeleton→live re-derivation and the new `selectPath` wrapper (replacing the raw `setSelectedPath` prop) disarms it on an explicit file choice; `handleRepositoryChange` calls the new `gitWorkflow.resyncDeskNavigation(live)` once on that transition, itself guarded on the desk for that root still being the active world. FolderPicker delays the row spinner by 80 ms (`openingSlowly`) while keeping `busy`/disabled immediate. `treeContentSyncMode` gained the root and a fourth mode `adopt` (reset without the collapse walk) so an open walks the directory list once instead of twice.

sections.summary: `openPatchWorld` now looks for an already-open patch world with the same `patchReviewIdentity(review)` (the PR URL) but a different worldId, carries its navigation entry over to the new world and dispatches `open-patch` with `supersedesWorldId`; `insertContentWorld` takes that id, replaces the superseded world in place (same tab slot) and treats it as a focus origin so `activeWorldId` is never left pointing at a removed world. Reopening a pull request after a force-push `replace` now lands on the tab that is already open.

sections.deviations: Chose supersede-and-rename over literally reusing the stale worldId. Reusing it would keep a worldId minted from the old oids, and the `replace-patch` reducer guard (`patchWorldId(action.review) === world.worldId`) would then silently drop the authoritative post-stream review. Superseding keeps the tab's slot, navigation and focus while every oid-keyed guard still matches.

sections.summary: `RepositoryWatcher` gained `pause()` (closes both fs.watch handles, clears the pending set and debounce timer, bumps the generation, keeps the snapshot), `resume()` (re-arms from the retained snapshot, returns whether it did) and a `paused` getter; `#schedule`/`#flush` bail while paused and handle closing is factored into `#closeHandles()`. The registry tracks `lastActiveAt` per session; `#setActiveRoot` pauses every other session's watcher, stamps and resumes the active one and — only when it had actually been paused — runs one refresh to catch it up; `#evictBeyondCap()` disposes least-recently-active sessions beyond MAX_RESIDENT_SESSIONS = 4, never the active root; `#parkBackgroundSession()` pauses a watcher armed for a repository opened with `activate=false`. `activate(root)` is now async and reopens a root the cap disposed instead of throwing, so a review world outliving its session recovers lazily.

sections.deviations: The plan's "fake watcher" is realised as `spyOn(RepositoryWatcher.prototype, …)` over real temp repositories — the registry constructs its watchers internally and adding an injection seam only for a test was not worth the API. `activate()` becoming async avoided any edit to the `activateRepository` IPC handler (not in Track E's index.ts ownership); its only production caller already returns a promise.

sections.summary: `capWorkspaceCache` is count-only now (MAX_CACHED_PATHS 20k→25k, MAX_CACHED_STATUSES 4k→5k, fileText 512 KB); `workspaceCacheBytes`, MAX_WORKSPACE_CACHE_BYTES and the stringify-and-halve loop are gone, and membership goes through a `Set` cached per path-array identity. Added a 3-slot LRU store (`WorkspaceCacheStore { version: 2, lastRoot, entries }`, `parseWorkspaceCacheStore` reading version-1 files as one slot, `workspaceCacheForRoot`, `lastWorkspaceCache`, `rememberWorkspaceCacheEntry`); the restore hint still carries only the last root and `getWorkspaceCache` still hands the renderer a single `WorkspaceCache`. `WorkspaceUiState` became a patch and the open file's text moved to its own `repository:file-text` channel, sent from a second 250 ms debounce keyed on `cachedFileTextIdentity` (path + main's sha1 `cacheKey`), so an unchanged file sends nothing. The disk write is debounced 1 s and atomic (temp + rename, temp removed on failure), never on the publish tick.

reviewNotes:
needs-owner (src/main/repository.ts — no Wave 3 track owns it): `RepositoryService.open` at ~line 1489 still does `const selectedRoot = await realpath(folderPath)`, so FO-11 is 4 resolutions down to 3, not 2. Exact edit: change the signature to `async open(folderPath: string, resolved = false)` with `const selectedRoot = resolved ? folderPath : await realpath(folderPath)`, and in repositorySessions.ts `open()` call `await repository.open(selectedRoot, true)` — the registry has always resolved `selectedRoot` by that point.

Riskiest spots, in order.
(1) P25 eviction can dispose a session that still has a background pull-request flight; `#stopSession` cancels it. With MAX_RESIDENT_SESSIONS = 4 and LRU ordering this needs five folders opened during one background fetch, and the world recovers through the new lazy `activate` → `open`, but it is a real behaviour change worth watching in the probe run. (2) `activate()` changed from sync-throwing to async-reopening; anything that relied on 'The repository tab is no longer open.' from that path now silently reopens instead. `require()` still throws for the other handlers, which is what the renderer's release flow expects. (3) P27 keeps the folder picker mounted for up to 400 ms after Enter; if a repository consistently loses main's 150 ms race the reader sees the picker sit there with a spinner for the remainder. Wave 2 measured 16-196 ms opens, so this should be rare, but it is the one visible UX change. (4) `resyncDeskNavigation` moves the selection and the view when the git snapshot lands; it is guarded on the desk for that root still being the active world and on `skeletonOpenRootRef`, which any explicit `selectPath` clears — but a non-user `onWorkspaceViewChange` (the explorer's own multi→file correction) does NOT disarm it, deliberately, so the live snapshot still wins over that correction.

Could not verify in-session: every probe target for these sections (open-folder `liveSnapshotMs`/`treeRowsMs`, the publish-handler median under 2 ms on core-3, `lsof | grep -c kqueue` staying flat across six opens, `windowShown` unchanged after the setImmediate). The build and install are Track F's, so nothing here was measured against the installed app. Two behaviours have no unit coverage by construction: the restore-hint memo and the deferred `beginSessionRestore` both live in index.ts, which has no test harness.

Two observations for the reviewer. The v2 cache file migrates v1 rather than discarding it, so an existing `last-workspace.json` still paints on the first launch after this lands; the first save rewrites it as a store. And `insertContentWorld`'s new supersede clause had a null-vs-null bug in my first pass (`activeWorldId === supersedesWorldId` is true when both are null, which would have let a background `open-patch` steal focus) — caught in self-review, guarded on `supersedesWorldId != null`, and pinned by a new reducer test.

One transient, not mine: at 16:00:31 `bun run lint` reported two unused-import warnings in src/renderer/src/CommandPaletteHost.dom.test.tsx (file mtime nine seconds before the run) — another track mid-edit. They were gone by the final run.
